text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Thursday's Pakistani newspapers:
- The Karachi Stock Exchange has decided to put 100 companies in the counter of defaulter companies for violating listing rules and regulations.
- Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari has signed a memorandum of understanding with South Korean company Daewoo Chairman Young-Soo Chang for investment in Pakistan.

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto rejected the idea of a consensus government run by technocrats and unelected people and sought the opposition's cooperation to strengthen the system and recover 95 billion rupees in stuck-up loans.
- Police are confused about the mysterious murder of a Buddhist monk found slain in the pagoda of the Sri Lankan embassy in Islamabad.

- The government is working on a comprehensive policy package to negotiate with the International Monetary Fund on the eve of its annual meeting in Washington, said V.A. Jafarey, special adviser to Bhutto on finance and economic affairs.
- The Privatisation Commission is likely to hire a financial adviser for United Bank Ltd.
- The French government has shown willingness to help fund the food processing departments of various universities.
- The State (central) Bank has barred commercial banks from providing financing facilities to modaraba (Islamic mutual fund) companies without its prior permission.
- At least 231,848 (275-lb) bales of raw cotton have arrived in the market at the start of ginning season.
- Sugar importers are expecting the government to withdraw 10 percent regulatory duty on sugar imports.
